chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār said: Abū ʿAlī ibn Rāshid said to me:

I said to him: You ordered me to undertake your affair and to take your due right, so I informed your followers of that. Then some of them said to me: What thing is his right? So I did not know what I should answer him with.

He said: khums is obligatory upon them. I said: In what thing? He said: In their goods and their estates, and upon the merchant according to his trade, and the craftsman by his hand; and that is when it is possible for them after their expenses.

key_terms.التَّاجِرِ: the merchant, meaning one who earns through trade
key_terms.الصَّانِعِ: the craftsman or artisan who earns by manual work
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth tax that is obligatory on qualifying gains
key_terms.حَقِّكَ: your due right, referring here to the Imam’s entitled share
key_terms.مَئُونَتِهِمْ: their expenses or necessary living costs

ai.seo_question: On what kinds of earnings and property is khums obligatory according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that khums is obligatory on certain forms of gain and property. It clarifies that this applies to goods, estates, trade income, and the earnings of craftsmen, when there remains ability after covering expenses.
